https://www.politico.eu/article/sebastie.text: PARIS — French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said his government’s budget for 2027 will include a staggering €54 billion in savings as he attempts to contain the country’s growing deficit in a year that’s seen little to no economic growth. In an excerpt of an interview published by French daily Le Figaro , Lecornu said that without any cuts, the budget deficit would spike to 6.5% of gross domestic product — making it all but impossible for the government to keep its promise to the European Commission to get that figure to 3% of GDP by 2029. “These savings will serve to considerably curb the growth of spending, which has been rising inexorably year after year” due to an aging population which increases health and old-age-related costs, Lecornu added. Advertisement Advertisement France has in recent years struggled to rein in spending and a debt burden that has grown from €2.3 trillion to more than €3.5 trillion and is becoming increasingly expensive to service as interest rates spike across the world. Lecornu, who vigorously opposes tax hikes on any segments of the population, said the country needs to find an additional €10 billion to finance the debt. “The debt burden is weighing increasingly heavily on the budget equation,” he said. Lecornu said the 2027 budget deficit target was 5%, while the hope is to contain this year’s deficit to less than 5.5% The French government had initially planned on reducing its deficit to 4.7% of GDP this year — but acknowledged last week that the figure would ultimately land above 5%. It also cut its growth forecast for this year and next year to 0.5% in 2026 and 1% in 2027. The government targeted €30 billion in the 2026 budget and €60 billion the year prior. Lecornu’s minority government will present its budget bill to lawmakers in the coming weeks, but getting it passed will be difficult without a governing majority and as the spring 2027 presidential election gets closer, which will incentivize parties to stake out their positions ahead of an electoral cycle. https://www.politico.eu/article/russia-s.text: A Russian attack that killed at least 17 people including three children in Ukraine are Moscow’s “thanks for the lifting on sanctions on diesel exports,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday. A series of strikes on the south-eastern city of Zaporizhzhia also injured at least 18 people, including three children, Ukraine’s state emergency services said on Saturday afternoon . “People continue to be searched for under the rubble of destroyed houses. Rescue operations continue,” said Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of Zaporizhzhia regional military administration in a Telegram post . Advertisement Advertisement “Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia,” Zelenskyy said on X . The strikes took place just one day after U.S. President Donald Trump announced he would temporarily lift sanctions on Russian diesel in a bid to bring soaring prices down. Ukrainian officials were meeting on the same day with European and U.S. officials in Miami in a fresh diplomatic push to end the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Zelenskyy criticized the deal on Friday and accused Trump of using the peace talks as a “smokescreen” while pursuing a deal with the Kremlin. Even though the talks were supposed to last two days, the Ukrainian team decided to return home earlier then planned “because they managed to talk everything through earlier,” a senior official familiar with the matter told POLITICO. Ukraine will continue to bomb Russian oil refineries despite US-Russia deals, the official added. The Ukrainian armed forces said Saturday they struck a major oil facility in Russia’s Samara region overnight. Advertisement Advertisement Zelenskyy is currently busy coordinating with Europeans and preparing several high-level meetings, the official said. He spoke on Saturday with leaders of France , Norway and Finland . “Russian strikes killed over 80 Ukrainian civilians in two days. Moreover, it has stepped up its hybrid attacks against Europe, both EU Member States and NATO Allies,” Kaja Kallas, the EU’s foreign policy chief, said Saturday . “Suspending sanctions on Russian diesel provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war.” “On Monday, EU Foreign Ministers intend to approve the biggest set of sanctions listings targeting Russia’s war machine since the start of the war,” Kallas added.
